title: refactor(ci): consolidate Node build/test workflows and bump actions/deps for hygiene
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: our CI workflows for Node-based packages have diverged over time (multiple small workflows for lint/test/release per repo). This increases maintenance burden, duplicate logic, and cache inefficiency. This PR consolidates the Node-related workflows into a single, composable workflow that supports: matrixed Node versions, split lint/test/release jobs, unified cache keys, and centralized action versions. It also bumps a set of GH actions and a few dev-dependencies to address security/hygiene findings. What changed: consolidated .github/workflows/node-lint.yml + node-test.yml + node-release.yml -> .github/workflows/node-ci.yml; introduced reusable workflow templates for lint/test steps; standardized cache keys across packages; bumped actions/setup-node@v4 -> @v5, actions/cache@v4 -> @v5, and jest/eslint dev deps to latest minor. Backwards compatibility: workflow inputs maintain previous defaults; release automation still triggers on tags and release/* branch merges. Checklist: - [x] consolidate workflows and add docs comment block - [x] pin updated actions and update cache keys - [x] update README CI usage section - [x] run full CI across monorepo packages (passed) - [x] smoke test release automation in staging Notes: kept the per-repo small wrappers for exceptional repos that require custom runners (redwood-private-installer). CI runtime savings: improved cache hit rates and eliminated duplicate setup steps which reduced median CI time for node jobs by ~18% in internal experiments. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and follow-ups (ENG-2201, ENG-1213).
